_about: Voice picker catalogue for free_tts.py. A voice ID is '<engine>:<name>'. 'prompt' is the brief you append to a video's main prompt (PROMPT.md, 'Voice notes') when the user picks that voice. 'commercial': yes = licence allows it, no = non-commercial only, check = read the model card first. Licences checked June 2026; re-check before publishing.

edge.name: edge-tts (Microsoft neural voices)
edge.runtime: online - Microsoft Read Aloud service, any Python with edge-tts
edge.licence: code LGPL-3.0; voices under Microsoft service terms (unofficial endpoint - for paid/published work consider Azure AI Speech)
edge.prompt: Engine: edge-tts (online neural voice). Exact word timings come from the service. Punctuation is the only pacing control: '...' for a long beat, ',' for a short one. No SSML. Spell acronyms as said (A.I., S.Q.L.), write numbers as words, write 'Microsoft 365' not 'M365'. Never strand one word at the end of a sentence. Keep interjections plain ('Oh!' not 'Ooh!').

kokoro.name: Kokoro-82M (hexgrad) via kokoro-onnx
kokoro.install: pip install kokoro-onnx soundfile; download kokoro-v1.0.onnx + voices-v1.0.bin from https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx/releases into ~/tts-models/kokoro
kokoro.prompt: Engine: Kokoro-82M (offline, Apache-2.0). Very natural for its size, but prosody resets every sentence, so keep each clip to one to three short sentences (under ~30 words). It reads punctuation for pauses ('...' and ','); it does not do emotion on request, so put the feeling in the words. Spell out numbers, acronyms (A.I.) and brand names. Option speed (0.8-1.2, default 1.0) instead of rate; slow the narrator to 0.92-0.95.

piper.name: Piper (Open Home Foundation)
piper.runtime: offline CPU (tts-venv), real-time on a Raspberry Pi
piper.install: pip install piper-tts; voices from https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices into ~/tts-models/piper (<name>.onnx + .onnx.json)
piper.licence: code GPL-3.0; each voice has its own dataset licence (see the voice entry)
piper.prompt: Engine: Piper (offline, very fast). Clear but fairly even, 'smart speaker' delivery with little emotion, so it suits announcements, instructions, sat-nav and in-world devices more than drama. Use short declarative sentences and commas for breath. Spell out numbers and acronyms. Option length_scale (>1 slower, e.g. 1.1 for a calmer read).

kitten.name: Kitten TTS nano (KittenML)
kitten.install: pip install kittentts espeakng-loader (wheel from the GitHub releases)
kitten.prompt: Engine: Kitten TTS nano (tiny, offline). Slightly synthetic, gadget-like read - good for robots, apps, toys and side characters, not for the main narrator. It garbles one- and two-word inputs: every clip needs at least four words ('Okay, here we go.' not 'Okay!'). Keep lines short and plain; no unusual names.

supertonic.name: Supertonic (Supertone)
supertonic.licence: code MIT; model OpenRAIL-M (commercial use allowed with use-based restrictions)
supertonic.prompt: Engine: Supertonic (offline, 31 languages). Crisp, quick, slightly upbeat delivery. Great for multilingual lines: set lang (en, es, de, fr, ko, ja, ...) and write the line in that language. Keep sentences short; it handles numbers but spell out brand names. Pace with commas and full stops rather than long ellipses.

pocket.name: Pocket TTS (Kyutai)
pocket.runtime: offline CPU (tts-venv), faster than real time
pocket.licence: code MIT; model CC BY 4.0 (credit Kyutai); voices: see the voice entry
pocket.prompt: Engine: Pocket TTS by Kyutai (offline). Conversational and expressive, with natural breaths - the best free choice for characters talking to each other. Write lines the way people speak: contractions, short sentences, the odd 'Well,' or 'Right,'. Very short clips (one word) can come out clipped, so give each clip at least a short phrase. Credit 'Pocket TTS by Kyutai (CC BY 4.0)' in the description.

chatterbox.name: Chatterbox (Resemble AI)
chatterbox.runtime: offline CPU (cb-venv, own Python), slow: ~20 s to load, ~15-20 s per line
chatterbox.install: separate venv: python -m venv ~/cb-venv; ~/cb-venv/Scripts/pip install chatterbox-tts (or set CHATTERBOX_PY)
chatterbox.licence: MIT (code and weights); outputs carry a Perth watermark where the native watermarker is available
chatterbox.speed: slow - use for a few hero lines
chatterbox.prompt: Engine: Chatterbox by Resemble AI (offline, slow). The only free engine here with an emotion dial: exaggeration 0.25 = calm and measured, 0.5 = natural, 1.0-1.3 = very excited; lower cfg_weight (0.3) speeds it up and makes it more animated. Mark each line's emotion in the script and keep lines under ~25 words. It renders ~15-20 s per line on this laptop, so use it for a handful of hero lines, not a whole narration.

sapi.name: Windows SAPI desktop voices
sapi.install: nothing - ships with Windows (extra languages via Settings > Time & language > Speech)
sapi.prompt: Engine: Windows SAPI desktop voice (built in, offline). Deliberately robotic, early-2000s computer sound - use it as a joke or in-world machine (the old PC, a BSOD, a 'system announcement', a sat-nav), never as the main narrator. Short, flat sentences; spell everything out (numbers, A.I., Microsoft 365). Option rate (-10 to 10, default 0).

edge:andrew.prompt: Warm, trustworthy house narrator. Default pace -4%; trailer read -4%/-2Hz. Keep one narrator for the whole piece.

edge:ava.prompt: Bright, friendly and clear. Works as narrator or heroine; give her lines in the first person with feeling in the words ('Okay... I've got this.').

edge:emma.prompt: Upbeat ad-read energy. Short punchy sentences, a benefit per line.

edge:brian.prompt: Casual, relaxed colleague. Conversational phrasing, contractions.

edge:ryan-gb.prompt: Brisk, friendly British male. British spelling and idiom read naturally.

edge:wizard.prompt: Slow, grave mentor. Use '...' before the reveal word; pair with the 'wizard' FX chain (low shelf + hall reverb).

edge:darklord.prompt: Deep, measured villain. Short menacing sentences; pair with the 'vader' FX chain and keep its 2.8 kHz presence boost for intelligibility.

kokoro:af_heart.character: warm, natural (Kokoro's best voice, grade A)
kokoro:af_heart.prompt: Kokoro's most natural voice: warm and smooth. A strong free, offline narrator. Keep clips to one to three sentences.

kokoro:af_bella.prompt: Energetic and youthful. Good for an upbeat host; exclamation marks lift the read.

kokoro:af_nicole.prompt: Soft, breathy, close-mic delivery. Use for inner thoughts or a daydream aside, not for the main narration.

kokoro:am_michael.prompt: Steady, plain US male. A good neutral explainer narrator at speed 0.95.

kokoro:am_puck.prompt: Playful, cheeky sidekick. Give him quips and short reactions (at least a short phrase each).

kokoro:am_fenrir.prompt: Deeper, gruffer male. Blunt short sentences; works as a rival or grizzled expert.

kokoro:bm_george.prompt: Mature British documentary narrator. Measured, slightly formal phrasing ('And here, at last, ...'); speed 0.92-0.95 with '...' before reveals.

kokoro:bm_fable.prompt: British storyteller. Write in a 'once upon a time' cadence with ellipses on the turns.

kokoro:bm_lewis.prompt: Low, serious British male. Short weighty sentences.

kokoro:bf_emma.prompt: Clear, composed British female presenter. British spelling and idiom.

kokoro:bf_isabella.prompt: Lively British colleague. Conversational lines with contractions.

kokoro:ff_siwis.prompt: French female. Write the line in French; keep English brand names to a minimum.

kokoro:ef_dora.prompt: Spanish female. Write the line in Spanish.

piper:alan.prompt: Plain British male announcer. Use for in-world announcements and devices.

piper:northern.prompt: Down-to-earth northern English male. Plain, friendly lines; credit 'Piper northern_english_male (OpenSLR 83, CC BY-SA 4.0)'.

piper:lessac.prompt: Clear US female instruction voice. Step-by-step lines; internal/non-commercial use only.

piper:ryan.prompt: Clear US male announcer. Non-commercial only (CC BY-NC-SA).

kitten:4-f.prompt: Light, slightly synthetic female - an app or smart device talking. At least four words per clip.

kitten:3-m.prompt: Light synthetic male - a toy or robot sidekick. At least four words per clip.

kitten:5-m.prompt: Brighter synthetic male - an eager robot mascot. At least four words per clip.

supertonic:M1.prompt: Crisp male, quick delivery. Ideal when the same line is needed in several languages (set lang per line).

supertonic:M3.prompt: Deeper male. Set lang per line for non-English.

supertonic:F1.prompt: Clear female. Set lang per line for non-English.

supertonic:F2.prompt: Bright, upbeat female. Short exclamatory lines work well.

pocket:alba.licence: CC BY 4.0 (voice and model) - credit Kyutai
pocket:alba.prompt: Natural, conversational female with real breaths. Best for a heroine talking to colleagues.

pocket:javert.licence: CC0 voice / CC BY 4.0 model - credit Kyutai
pocket:javert.prompt: Natural, conversational male. Casual narrator or colleague; contractions and short sentences.

pocket:marius.prompt: Younger male side character. Check the voice licence before publishing.

chatterbox:excited.prompt: Over-the-top excited (exaggeration 1.3, cfg_weight 0.3). Use for one hype moment; write it with exclamation marks and repetition ('really, really').

chatterbox:clone.licence: MIT - consent of the cloned speaker required
chatterbox:clone.prompt: Voice clone of the reference clip (pass ref='path/to/clean_5-10s.wav'). Only clone a voice you have permission to use, and say so in the credits.

sapi:david.best_for: old PC, BSOD gag, system voice
sapi:david.prompt: Classic robotic Windows voice - the old PC or 'system' talking. Flat, literal lines.

sapi:zira.prompt: Robotic Windows female - a sat-nav or tannoy gag. Flat, literal lines.

sapi:hazel.prompt: Robotic British female system voice. Flat, literal lines.
